intro: Under the National Employment Standards, full-time and part-time employees have {fact:au_sick_leave_days} of paid sick and carer's leave each year, with part-timers getting a proportion. The page also covers what happens when paid leave runs out, how compassionate leave works and the separate leave for employees facing family and domestic violence.
explanation:
## Paid leave for sickness and caring

Full-time employees covered by the National Employment Standards (NES) get {fact:au_sick_leave_days} of paid sick and carer's leave each year, and part-time employees get a proportion of that. The employee can use it when they are unwell or hurt themselves, and also when someone in their immediate family or household needs care because of sickness, injury or an unexpected emergency. Whatever is not used in one year is still there the next. Casual employees do not get paid sick and carer's leave.

## Unpaid carer's leave and compassionate leave come on top of paid leave

Once a full-time or part-time employee has used up their paid sick and carer's leave, they can still take {fact:au_unpaid_carers_days} of carer's leave, unpaid. A casual employee's carer's leave is also unpaid, and the {fact:au_unpaid_carers_days} apply afresh every time a need for care arises.

Each time an immediate family or household member dies or has a life-threatening illness or injury, the employee can take {fact:au_compassionate_days} of compassionate leave. It also covers a stillbirth and some miscarriages. Full-time and part-time employees are paid their base pay rate for it, while casual employees take it unpaid. It does not build up over time and is separate from sick and carer's leave.

## Family and domestic violence leave

Paid family and domestic violence (FDV) leave covers casual, part-time and full-time employees alike, at {fact:au_fdv_leave_days} a year. Working part-time or casually does not reduce the entitlement. It is there from the first day of work, and each work anniversary restores it to the full amount, with nothing carried over from the year before. FDV leave is available to the employee who is experiencing the violence, not to someone supporting another person through it. They can use it to deal with the effects when that cannot reasonably be done outside work hours.

## Awards and agreements can add to it

An award, agreement or contract cannot give less than these standards, and any term that does has no effect. Such documents can add to the standards and can set some rules for how they work. For example, they can allow paid sick and carer's leave to be cashed out, or let an employee give up some pay in return for extra sick and carer's or annual leave.
meta_description: Sick and carer's leave in Australia: {fact:au_sick_leave_days} paid, plus carer's and compassionate leave and {fact:au_fdv_leave_days} of paid family and domestic violence leave.
